newsitem.title: FRANCE: CENTRE-RIGHT WOULD WIN FRENCH ELECTION NOW -POLL.
newsitem.headline: CENTRE-RIGHT WOULD WIN FRENCH ELECTION NOW -POLL.

text.p: France's ruling centre-right coalition would lose about 150 seats but retain a parliamentary majority if a general election were held now, an opinion poll published on Monday showed.

The SOFRES poll, in the daily newspaper Le Figaro, appeared hours before President Jacques Chirac was expected to dissolve the National Assembly and call early parliamentary elections for late May or early June -- nine months ahead of schedule.
The survey, conducted last Thursday and Friday, found the Gaullist-dominated coalition would lose about 150 of the 478 seats it now holds in the 577-member Assembly elected in 1993.
But it would hold 318 seats, giving it a comfortable lower house majority, the poll of 1,000 adults found.
The survey showed some 60 percent of voters said they had already made up their minds who to vote for, while 40 percent said they could still change their minds.

No official statement has yet been made but France's media said Chirac would make a televised address at 8.00 p.m. (1800 GMT) calling a two-round election which would be held on May 25-June 1 or June 1-8.

Analysts said Chirac wanted to get the election out of the way now, rather than have to campaign next year at a time of possibly unpopular austerity measures to enable France to qualify for a single European currency.

The poll indicated the following breakdown in seats if an election were held now: centre-right coalition, 318, Socialists, ecologists and other non-communist left-wing groups, 208, Communists, 27 and rightist National Front (FN), two.
France's electoral system is such that the FN has no seats in the assembly now despite commanding the votes of up to 15 percent of the electorate.
Following is the line-up of France's 577-member National Assembly, expected to be dissolved by President Jacques Chirac on Monday for a snap parliamentary general election:
- Rally for the Republic (RPR - Gaullists): 242 plus 16 allied for a total of 258 deputies.
- Union for French Democracy (UDF - centre-right): 200 plus six allied for a total of 206 deputies.
- Socialist Party: 56 plus seven allied for a total of 63 deputies.
- Communist Party: 22 members plus two allied for total of 24.
- Republic and Liberty group (independents of both left and right): 23.
